activity.notes: Adud al-Dawla was installed at Shiraz in 949 as successor to Imad al-Dawla and ruled Fars until the expansion of his direct rule into Iraq in 977. The mod's Daylam label reflects Buyid Daylamite origin, not a separate kingdom of Daylam ruled throughout his career.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica — ʿAŻOD-AL-DAWLA, ABŪ ŠOJĀʾ FANNĀ ḴOSROW
sources.citation_text: Iranica describes Adud al-Dawla's installation on the throne of Fars at Shiraz in 949 and his subsequent expansion of power.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica — Fārs iii. History in the Islamic Period
sources.citation_text: Iranica states that Adud al-Dawla ruled Fars from 949 to 977 and Fars together with Iraq from 977 to 983.

review_context.correction_note: Represent the Buyid Fars phase rather than an ethnic Daylam polity.
